relations.definition: A person or organization involved in an event
relations.embedding_query_text: participant: A person or organization involved in an event

instances: Neymar -> Brazil vs Norway Round of 16 Match

chosen_property.label: attendee
chosen_property.justification: The inverse of 'attendee' (Event → Person/Organization) fits the observed Person → Event pairs where the participant is involved in the event, even though schema.org's 'attendee' typically denotes presence. No as_is candidate aligns with the phrase's direction.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: sportsTeam
candidates.comment: A participation relation between an exercise action and the sports team involved in it. Also called "team participated", "team involved", "athletic team". Examples: "The goal was scored by the sportsTeam Real Madrid", "The race involved sportsTeam Team USA", "This action was performed by a sportsTeam.". Distinct from participant, which is a more general participant property.

relations.definition: An event that directly leads to another event
relations.embedding_query_text: cause: An event that directly leads to another event

instances: Brazil vs Norway Round of 16 Match -> Neymar Announces International Retirement

chosen_property.label: source
chosen_property.justification: The 'source' property (InstantaneousEvent → Thing) matches the InternationalMatch → InternationalRetirementAnnouncement pairing as a causal originator.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: lifeEvent
candidates.comment: A life event relation between a person and a significant event in their life. Also called: significant event, personal milestone, biographical event. Examples: "John Doe lifeEvent Baptism", "Jane Smith lifeEvent Graduation Ceremony", "Family lifeEvent Wedding".

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

chosen_property.justification: The 'hasCredential' property (Organization/Person → Credential) fits the Person → CareerStatistics pairing as a career-related credential.

candidates.label: playersOnline
candidates.comment: A quantitative attribute indicating the current number of players connected to a game server. Also called active players, concurrent players, player count. Examples: A game server has 150 players online. The server shows 2000 players online. A specific instance has 10 players online.

candidates.label: athlete
candidates.comment: A person who is a performing member of a sports team. Also called: player, team member, sportsman/sportswoman. Examples: "SportsTeam 'Lakers' athlete 'LeBron James'", "SportsTeam 'Red Sox' athlete 'Mookie Betts'", "SportsTeam 'National Team' athlete 'Megan Rapinoe'". Distinct from coach, which is a non-playing role.

candidates.label: numberOfPlayers
candidates.comment: The number of people who can play a game or video game series, often expressed as a minimum, maximum, or range. Also called player count, game capacity, participant number. Examples: "Board Game X numberOfPlayers '2-4'", "Video Game Y numberOfPlayers '1 (single-player)'", "Online Game Z numberOfPlayers '100 (max)'".

candidates.label: agentInteractionStatistic
candidates.comment: An agent interaction statistic relation between an organization or person and a counter representing their completed interactions in a specific agent role and context. Also called interaction count, activity metric, engagement statistic. Examples: "A customer service agent's interaction statistic shows '150 calls handled'.", "A company's agent interaction statistic indicates '1000 sales completed'."

candidates.label: statType
candidates.comment: A classification of a statistical variable by the type of statistic it represents, such as mean or count. Also called "statistic type", "measurement type", "data type", "statistical measure". Examples: "The variable has statType mean", "This statistical variable's statType is count", "The statType indicates a median value."

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: interactionStatistic
candidates.comment: An interaction metric relation between a creative work, organization, or person, and a counter that quantifies user interactions with it. Also called engagement metrics, user activity, interaction data, usage statistics. Examples: A blog post has an interactionStatistic of a 'LikeAction' counter. An organization has an interactionStatistic of a 'CommentAction' counter. A person has an interactionStatistic of a 'ShareAction' counter.

candidates.label: diseaseSpreadStatistics
candidates.comment: A disease spread statistics relation between a special announcement and a dataset, observation, URL, or web content containing statistical information about the spread of a disease. Also called "epidemic data", "infection rates", "case statistics". Examples: "Special announcement diseaseSpreadStatistics 'Dataset of daily cases'", "Public health update diseaseSpreadStatistics 'WebContent on regional spread'", "COVID-19 alert diseaseSpreadStatistics 'URL to dashboard'".

candidates.label: numberedPosition

Examples: "Athlete Role numberedPosition 23", "Team Member Role numberedPosition 7", "Employee Role numberedPosition 101". Distinct from namedPosition, which is a textual name for a role.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: geographicArea
candidates.comment: A geographic area relation between an audience and the administrative area it is associated with. Also called: target region, audience location, demographic area. Examples: "Local News Audience" geographic area "Springfield County", "National Election Voters" geographic area "United States", "European Market Audience" geographic area "European Union".

candidates.label: spatialCoverage
candidates.comment: A geographic focus relation between a creative work and the place(s) that are the primary subject or focus of its content. Also called "geographic scope", "covered area", "location focus", "content location". Examples: "A weather dataset has spatialCoverage New York State", "The historical map's spatialCoverage is ancient Rome", "This research paper's spatialCoverage is the Arctic region.". Distinct from spatial, which is a more general spatial association when the specific focus is not known.

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: longitude

Examples: "Eiffel Tower longitude 2.2945", "Statue of Liberty longitude -74.0445", "Mount Everest longitude 86.9250".

candidates.label: announcementLocation
candidates.comment: An announcement location relation between a special announcement and the specific civic structure or local business it pertains to. Also called relevant location, associated place, specific venue. Examples: "A special announcement's announcement location is 'City Hall'.", "The emergency announcement's announcement location is 'Local Grocery Store'." Distinct from spatialCoverage, which is used for larger geographic regions.

candidates.label: studyLocation
candidates.comment: A geographic relation between a medical study and the administrative area where it is conducted or was conducted. Also called "research location", "trial site", "study area", "geographic scope of study". Examples: "The medical study has studyLocation New York", "The clinical trial's studyLocation is Europe", "This study is taking place in a specific studyLocation."

chosen_property.label: scheduledTime

candidates.label: scheduledTime

Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: exceptDate
candidates.comment: An exception date relation between a schedule and a specific date or datetime when a scheduled event will not take place. Also called: exclusion date, cancelled date, unavailable date. Examples: "Weekly Yoga Class Schedule" except date "2023-12-25", "Daily Bus Route Schedule" except date "2024-01-01T08:00:00", "Monthly Book Club Schedule" except date "2023-11-11".

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: scheduledPaymentDate
candidates.comment: The specific date on which an invoice is planned or expected to be paid. Also called payment due date, invoice due date, planned payment date. Examples: `Invoice #123` scheduledPaymentDate `2023-12-31`, `Utility Bill` scheduledPaymentDate `2024-01-15`, `Consulting Invoice` scheduledPaymentDate `2023-11-30`. Distinct from `paymentDueDate`, which is a more general term for when payment is due.

candidates.label: byDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the week on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "days of week", "weekly recurrence", "on day". Examples: "Weekly meeting schedule byDay Monday", "Class schedule byDay 'MO,WE,FR'".

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: byMonth
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the month(s) of the year on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "months of year", "monthly recurrence", "in month". Examples: "Annual conference schedule byMonth 10", "Quarterly report schedule byMonth 3,6,9,12".

candidates.label: endDate

Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: eventSchedule
candidates.comment: An event schedule relation between an event and a schedule that defines a series of repeating occurrences for it. Also called "recurring schedule", "event timetable", "series schedule". Examples: "Gym class eventSchedule 'Weekly schedule for Yoga'", "Concert series eventSchedule 'Schedule for monthly performances'", "Webinar series eventSchedule 'Schedule for bi-weekly sessions'". A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

relations.definition: A country winning a medal in an international competition
relations.embedding_query_text: won_medal: A country winning a medal in an international competition

chosen_property.label: award
chosen_property.justification: The 'award' property (CreativeWork/Person → Text) fits the OlympicMedal → Country pairing as a recognition won by the country.

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: award
candidates.comment: An award won by or for a creative work, organization, person, product, or service. Also called: honor, prize, recognition. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' award 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' award 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' award 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from awards, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: awards
candidates.comment: Awards won by or for a creative work, organization, person, or product. Also called: honors, prizes, recognitions. Examples: "CreativeWork 'Movie' awards 'Oscar'", "Organization 'Company X' awards 'Best Employer'", "Person 'Scientist' awards 'Nobel Prize'". Distinct from award, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: returnPolicyCountry
candidates.comment: The country designated as the destination for product returns under a merchant return policy. Also called return destination country, country for returns, return shipping country. Examples: `US Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `"US"`, `European Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `Country: Germany`, `International Return Policy` returnPolicyCountry `"CA"`.

candidates.label: countryOfAssembly
candidates.comment: A manufacturing location relation between a product and the country where it was assembled. Also called: assembled in, manufacturing country, assembly location. Examples: "Smartphone" country of assembly "China", "Car" country of assembly "Mexico", "Laptop" country of assembly "Vietnam". Distinct from countryOfOrigin, which refers to the country of the principal offices or where the product originates.

candidates.label: sport
candidates.comment: An identification of the type of sport associated with a sports event or organization. Also called "sport type", "athletic discipline", "game played". Examples: "The event's sport is Basketball", "The organization's sport is Soccer", "This competition features the sport of Gymnastics."

candidates.label: nationality
candidates.comment: A country representing the nationality of a person. Also called citizenship, country of origin, national identity. Examples: "Person A nationality 'United States'", "Person B nationality 'France'", "Person C nationality 'Japan'". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the location where a person was born.

chosen_property.label: contentReferenceTime
chosen_property.justification: The 'contentReferenceTime' property (CreativeWork → DateTime) matches the Tournament → Year pairing as the temporal context of the event.

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: foodEstablishment
candidates.comment: A food establishment relation between a cook action and the specific place or food establishment where the cooking occurred. Also called: cooking location, restaurant, kitchen. Examples: "Chef prepares meal" food establishment "Gourmet Restaurant", "Home Cook makes dinner" food establishment "My Kitchen", "Baker bakes bread" food establishment "Local Bakery". Distinct from foodEvent, which is a specific event.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".
